Pride
PRYD
noun
The inordinate exaltation of self; from the Old English pryde, haughtiness; the root sin of the fallen heart.

See also: Pride · Pride

📖 Biblical Definition

Pride is the inordinate exaltation of self—the lifting up of the heart against God and above one’s fellow men—and Scripture treats it as the root and mother of sin. It was pride that cast down the anointed cherub, who said in his heart, I will be like the most High; pride that the serpent stirred in Eve with the promise, ye shall be as gods; pride that is the first of the things the LORD hates, a proud look heading the list of seven abominations. The fear of the LORD is to hate evil, and chiefly pride, arrogancy, and the froward mouth, which God hates. Pride goes before destruction, and a haughty spirit before a fall; the pride of life is not of the Father but of the world. Above all, pride sets a man against the grace of God, for God resists the proud but gives grace unto the humble—the proud heart will not stoop to receive salvation as a free gift, insisting on its own worth and its own way. The dictionary reads pride as the original and besetting sin, the self set up where God should be, the spring of unbelief, rebellion, and contempt of others; and it answers pride with the humility that the gospel both requires and works—the bowing of the self before God, who gives His grace to the lowly and brings down everyone that is proud and lifted up.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

The inordinate exaltation of self against God and above men; the root sin of the fallen heart, which God resists, answered by the humility the gospel works.

PRIDE, the inordinate exaltation of self against God and above men.

The root and mother of sin, from the fall of the cherub to the fall of Eve.

Pride goeth before destruction, an haughty spirit before a fall (Pro 16:18).

📖 Key Scripture

Pro 16:18 — "Pride goeth before destruction, and an haughty spirit before a fall."

Jas 4:6 — "But he giveth more grace. Wherefore he saith, God resisteth the proud, but giveth grace unto the humble."

Pro 8:13 — "The fear of the LORD is to hate evil: pride, and arrogancy, and the evil way, and the froward mouth, do I hate."

1Jo 2:16 — "For all that is in the world, the lust of the flesh, and the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life, is not of the Father, but is of the world."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

The age makes pride a virtue—self-esteem, self-assertion, self-celebration—and renames humility as weakness; Scripture names pride the root sin that God resists and humility the grace He gives.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The corruption to name is the modern celebration of pride as a virtue. The age exalts self-esteem, self-assertion, and self-love as the keys to flourishing, and rebrands the very pride Scripture calls the root sin as confidence and authenticity, while sneering at humility as weakness or self-hatred. Whole movements parade the word “pride” as a banner. But God’s verdict does not change: a proud look is the first of the things He hates, pride goes before destruction, and God resists the proud. To call the chief of sins a virtue is to bless the very thing that ruins the soul and bars it from grace.

The principle to recover is the sinfulness of pride and the grace of humility. Pride is the self set up where God should be—the spring of unbelief that will not receive salvation as a gift, of rebellion that will not submit, of contempt that despises others. It must be put to death. God resists the proud but gives grace to the humble; the gospel both requires humility and works it, bowing the sinner to receive Christ and clothing the saint with lowliness. The way up is down: he that humbleth himself shall be exalted, and the lowly find the grace the proud forfeit.
